verbalization: Goiazensolide appears to exert its biological effects through a series of interconnected molecular pathways that ultimately target the PITSLRE serine/threonine-protein kinase CDC2L1. The evidence suggests that Goiazensolide acts as a broad inhibitor of protein kinases, with a direct interaction with the target kinase CDC2L1. This is supported by the presence of a specific target molecule, (10S,13R,14R,15S,17R)-15-hydroxy-17-[(2R)-7-hydroxy-6-(hydroxymethyl)hept-5-en-2-yl]-4,4,10,13,14-pentamethyl-1,2,5,6,12,15,16,17-octahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-3-one, which is known to be a substrate of the kinase. This indicates that Goiazensolide may inhibit the kinase activity through a direct or indirect mechanism, possibly by modulating the phosphorylation of the target protein. Additionally, the presence of another target, Protein kinase C eta, which is also a substrate of the kinase, further supports the notion that Goiazensolide influences multiple kinases in the pathway. The integration of these findings suggests that Goiazensolide may act as a broad-acting kinase inhibitor, with potential implications for cellular processes involving the CDC2L1 kinase. The mechanism is supported by the presence of a known substrate of the kinase, which provides a direct link between the drug and the target protein.
